title: Activation Fastpath — KPI checklist & capacity notes
summary: Working doc for a "fastpath" activation flow: lightweight readiness checklist + compact KPI set and short-form capacity notes for features that need deterministic latency under bursty traffic. Purpose is to give product and ops a 10–15 minute checklist for go/no-go and a small capacity playbook to prebook Dedicated slots or enable immediate fallback routing.
objective: Enable predictable first-wave launches for latency-sensitive features by codifying minimal KPIs, capacity safety margins, and quick escalation steps. Reduce decision time during early live traffic spikes.
checklist: Preflight: confirm canary traffic target (default 1% or 500 rps, whichever is lower)
SLA gating: p95 latency baseline <= 150ms on beta dataset for 1k seq length
Model pin: exact model hash and quantization profile documented in release PR
Capacity: reserved Dedicated pool (min 2 x 80GB A100 equiv) OR confirmed fallback variant with <20% quality delta
Observability: dashboard wired (token-level) with error, latency, and cost tiles; alert thresholds configured
Rollout policy: slow-roll over 72 hours with traffic doubling every 8 hrs, explicit rollback condition(s)
Canary evaluation: run prompt set SLO suite; run A/B head-to-head for quality drift
Oncall: primary + secondary owned and paged for the first 36h, escalation matrix attached
Communication: launch Slack channel and status doc stub created
Postmortem owner assigned before traffic >5k users
capacity_notes: Target initial capacity: 2 GPU workers sized to support 1.5x expected peak (baseline = forecasted 2k reqs/min for beta)
Recommended pool: Dedicated-preemptible not allowed for fastpath; reserve non-preemptible with burst policy + 30% headroom
Autoscale policy: vertical burst (add worker) on queue depth > 150 for 60s, scale down after 600s stable
KV cache warming: pre-warm prefixes from top 50 prompts; if cache miss rate > 20% after 30m, throttle new users
Fallback strategy: active-model fallback to 7B quantized variant with cached prefixes; route only if P95 > 220ms or error rate spike detected
Runbook snippet: if p95 > 250ms for 3 consecutive 5m windows, drop traffic to 10% and notify SRE
simulation_scenarios: Baseline: 2k reqs/min steady - p95 132ms, success 99.7%, cost per 1k tokens $0.27
3x spike (burst 6k reqs/min for 15m) - if no burst capacity, p95 climbs to 280ms; fallback reduces quality -0.9pt but keeps success rate 99.0%
Cold-start test: full deploy from zero cache - initial 20m average p95 210ms decreasing to 140ms after 25m of warmup
Network partition (region fallback) - routed 40% to secondary region; observed 12% higher token cost but p95 maintained under 200ms
